values: In modern everyday French, « embrasser quelqu’un » most often means to kiss someone; the older sense “to embrace” remains context-dependent.
« Emmener » means to take a person or animal along to another place; use « emporter » for taking an object away.
« Emporter » is normally used for taking an object away; « emmener » is preferred for taking a person or animal along.
« Emprunter quelque chose à quelqu’un » means to borrow something from someone; the verb also applies to taking a route or means of transport.
« Engager quelqu’un » means to hire someone; « s’engager à + infinitif » means to commit or promise to do something.
« Enlever » can mean to remove or take away; with clothing, it means to take off, while « s’enlever » describes something coming off.
« Entendre » means to hear, whereas « écouter » means to listen actively; « s’entendre avec » means to get along with someone.
Use « envisager de + infinitif » when considering a possible action.
Affirmative « espérer que » normally takes the indicative, unlike many expressions of emotion or uncertainty.

batch_summary: Clarified several easily confused verbs and added missing common senses and constructions.
